# Working in this repository

GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.

## Commands

On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
```

# GraphGoblin Documentation

Last full revision: 2026-10-07. These are living documents. Update them as decisions change, and record each material change as an ADR under `decisions/`.

GraphGoblin is a progressive web application plus a gateway backend for designing, running, and observing agent **loops**. A loop is a graph of nodes. Triggers start it. Decision nodes route it. Inferencing nodes hand work to an agent harness. Script and context-mutation nodes shape the shared **context thread**. Wait and heartbeat nodes park it. Subloops nest it. An exit node decides when it is done, what it returns, and where the result goes.

GraphGoblin is built for AI engineers. AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC) pipelines are the first use case, not the only one. Nothing in the core should assume GitHub, pull requests, or software engineering.

## Reading order

| #   | Document                                                     | What it covers                                                                                                  |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| -   | [User guide](guide/README.md)                                | Install locally, build loops, run and observe, configure triggers and integrations                              |
| 01  | [Vision and scope](01-vision-and-scope.md)                   | Purpose, target users, mental model, principles, 1.0 scope, post-1.0 roadmap                                    |
| 02  | [Architecture](02-architecture.md)                           | Stack, layering, package layout, ports, process topology, cross-cutting concerns                                |
| -   | [Architecture snapshot](architecture/README.md)              | Structural map of the code at `c379f80`: packages, data, storage, API, web, adapters, triggers, one traced loop |
| -   | [Debt register](architecture/debt-register.md)               | Technical debt items, reconciled issues, prioritized follow-ups and owner decisions (#163)                      |
| 03  | [Domain model](03-domain-model.md)                           | Loops, versions, nodes, runs, events, invocations, the context thread                                           |
| 04  | [Node catalog](04-node-catalog.md)                           | Every node type: purpose, configuration, ports, engine behaviour                                                |
| 05  | [Execution engine](05-execution-engine.md)                   | Executor semantics, event sourcing, run lifecycle, resiliency model                                             |
| 06  | [Harness integration](06-harness-integration.md)             | Harness port, Codex/Claude/Ollama inference, model discovery and Chat workflow integration                      |
| 07  | [API, streaming, and MCP](07-api-and-streaming.md)           | REST surface, SSE, OpenAPI, auth, MCP server, Codex and Claude Code plugins                                     |
| 08  | [Triggers and integrations](08-triggers-and-integrations.md) | Manual, cron, webhook, inbound event, polling; security of inbound paths                                        |
| 09  | [Frontend and PWA](09-frontend-and-pwa.md)                   | Native Chat, paired Goblin PWA, editor, run inspector, settings and service-worker update flow                  |
| 10  | [Testing and quality](10-testing-and-quality.md)             | Coverage policy, fixtures, adversarial QA agents, CI gates                                                      |
| 11  | [Security and distribution](11-security-and-distribution.md) | Licensing, credentials, secrets, inbound exposure, retention                                                    |
| 12  | [Implementation plan](12-implementation-plan.md)             | Milestones M0 to M8 with tasks and acceptance criteria                                                          |
| 13  | [Open questions](13-open-questions.md)                       | Items that still need a decision, and which milestone they block                                                |
| 14  | [Work packages](14-work-packages.md)                         | Delegated work packages, delivery waves, and acceptance criteria from M3 onward                                 |
| 15  | [Issue workflow](15-issue-workflow.md)                       | Issue gates, QA scope, model routing, milestones, and this repository's development pipeline                    |
| -   | [Delivery register](delivery/2026-10-18-i01-i07-register.md) | Decisions, ownership, review findings, evidence and continuation notes for the dispatched intents I01 to I07    |
| -   | [reference/nodes.md](reference/nodes.md)                     | Node config reference, generated from the schemas (`pnpm docs:generate`)                                        |
| -   | [reference/api.md](reference/api.md)                         | REST API reference, generated from the OpenAPI document                                                         |
| -   | [decisions/](decisions/)                                     | Architecture decision records                                                                                   |
| -   | [research/](research/)                                       | Preserved research on Codex, Claude Code, Jev, licences, and runtimes                                           |

## Status legend

Every section, node, or decision carries one of these labels.

- **Decided**: agreed with the product owner. Change it through a new ADR.
- **Draft**: proposed by the architect and not yet confirmed. Build to the proposed shape and expect revision.
- **Open**: needs a decision before the dependent milestone starts. Tracked in `13-open-questions.md`.

## Conventions

- "1.0" is the first usable release for a single-user laptop. "Post-1.0" items are recorded because they shape the design today, not because they are being built now.
- Vocabulary is defined once in `03-domain-model.md`: loop, loop version, node, port, edge, run, invocation, context thread, harness, return channel.
- Code in these docs is a sketch that shows shape, not a final API. Once `packages/contracts` exists, its Zod schemas are the source of truth and the docs follow them.

Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.

## Commands

On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
```

# GraphGoblin Documentation

Last full revision: 2026-10-07. These are living documents. Update them as decisions change, and record each material change as an ADR under `decisions/`.

GraphGoblin is a progressive web application plus a gateway backend for designing, running, and observing agent **loops**. A loop is a graph of nodes. Triggers start it. Decision nodes route it. Inferencing nodes hand work to an agent harness. Script and context-mutation nodes shape the shared **context thread**. Wait and heartbeat nodes park it. Subloops nest it. An exit node decides when it is done, what it returns, and where the result goes.

GraphGoblin is built for AI engineers. AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC) pipelines are the first use case, not the only one. Nothing in the core should assume GitHub, pull requests, or software engineering.

## Reading order

## Status legend

Every section, node, or decision carries one of these labels.

- **Decided**: agreed with the product owner. Change it through a new ADR.
- **Draft**: proposed by the architect and not yet confirmed. Build to the proposed shape and expect revision.
- **Open**: needs a decision before the dependent milestone starts. Tracked in `13-open-questions.md`.

## Conventions

- "1.0" is the first usable release for a single-user laptop. "Post-1.0" items are recorded because they shape the design today, not because they are being built now.
- Vocabulary is defined once in `03-domain-model.md`: loop, loop version, node, port, edge, run, invocation, context thread, harness, return channel.

1	# 15 - Issue workflow
2	
3	GitHub issues are the shared work queue for this repository's development pipeline. Every non-epic issue carries at least one gate label. A triager sets the type, area, gate, QA, and routing labels from the issue and its dependencies.
4	
5	## Gates
6	
7	- `aidlc-ready`: the issue may enter this repository's agent-led development pipeline. Its approved behaviour is accepted through independent agent review, tests appropriate to the acceptance criteria and independent QA: tests through public methods that directly establish a criterion are sufficient for that criterion, and API, native-process or browser evidence is added where a criterion needs it. Use for bug fixes, maintainability, chores, backend work and ordinary testable feature and UI work.
8	- `human-in-the-loop`: the work is implemented, reviewed, tested and merged through the same agent gates, and in addition a human exercises the merged build afterwards and records what they observed. Reserve it for feature work with substantial ambiguity, or behaviour whose correctness agents cannot readily verify with confidence. A UI change does not qualify merely because it changes a screen; a missing or failing test, or a known defect, is engineering work, not a reason for the label. Before applying it, record on the issue the feature, the specific ambiguity or verification limit, what public-interface tests and other agent evidence establish, and a concrete post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations. The label does not require a human review before merge and waives no technical gate.
9	- `needs-plan-approval`: for architecture changes and cutovers. An agent posts a written plan as an issue comment. A human approves by replacing this label with `plan-approved` and adding `aidlc-ready`, keeping `human-in-the-loop` when it applies.
10	- `plan-approved`: set by a human only, after reviewing the written plan.
11	
12	`aidlc-ready` describes delivery eligibility and `human-in-the-loop` describes a later human QA obligation, so the two may coexist; `needs-plan-approval` may be combined with either. Until 2026-10-21 this file described `human-in-the-loop` as a human review of the running product before merge, classified UI work under it as a whole and said it never combined with `aidlc-ready`. That wording was this repository's own metadata, not an owner requirement for objectively verifiable behaviour; the owner's clarification of 2026-10-21 (recorded in [#279](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/279)) supersedes it.
13	
14	## Post-merge human QA
15	
16	Every pull request for a `human-in-the-loop` issue carries a post-merge human QA checklist with expected observations and names an open tracking item (the issue itself or a linked QA item). The PR references that item as "Part of", never with a closing keyword, so the pipeline never closes it. After the merge a human exercises the merged build, records the commit or build, their observations and the outcome on the tracking item, and closes it. Human QA is tracked separately from implementation, review, agent QA, CI and merge, as one of: not required, pending merge, pending human QA, or completed with an evidence link. Agent evidence never completes the human step, and the human step never permits merging a known defect or bypassing a gate. A product decision that is needed to define correct behaviour goes to the owner as a concrete question with evidence, separately from post-merge QA.
17	
18	A delivery batch may carry an additional pre-merge sign-off gate (for example, a designated independent review session that must approve each PR at an exact head). Such a gate is recorded in the batch's register under `docs/delivery/` and is separate from post-merge human QA.
19	
20	## Parking markers
21	
22	Two labels take an issue out of the queue; neither is a gate, and an issue carrying one has no gate label until a human unparks it.
23	
24	- `backlog`: parked until further notice. Agents do not plan or implement it.
25	- `needs-refinement`: the problem itself still needs human-driven refinement in a working session with the owner before any plan or implementation.
26	
27	## QA scope
28	
29	- `qa:touched-systems`: enumerate every system the change touches, test each with positive and negative cases, and record pass/fail results with evidence in both the PR and issue.
30	- `qa:full-regression`: also retest the whole application end to end, covering positive and negative scenarios, and catalogue the results.
31	
32	Name the QA agent in the issue body's Delivery section, not with a label.
33	
34	Retain QA evidence under `docs/qa/` with repository-relative citations and preserve raw JSON, YAML and JavaScript/TypeScript bytes so recorded hashes remain valid; `.prettierignore` excludes those artifacts while QA Markdown remains formatted.
35	
36	## Model routing
37	
38	The triager sets one `impl:<model>` label and one `review:<model>` label. Use the following tiers, with xhigh reasoning:
39	
40	| Tier | Model             | Use                         |
41	| ---- | ----------------- | --------------------------- |
42	| 1    | `gpt-6-luna`      | Mundane work                |
43	| 2    | `gpt-6.1-sol`     | Default work                |
44	| 3    | `claude-opus-5.5` | Harder work and sign-off    |
45	| 4    | `gpt-6-astra`     | Hardest work and escalation |
46	
47	Whatever model family implements the change, the other family reviews it: OpenAI models are reviewed by Claude, and Claude is reviewed by an OpenAI model. If a worker cannot finish, escalate to the next tier.
48	
49	## Types, areas, and milestones
50	
51	Every issue has one type: `type:bug`, `type:feature`, `type:ui-polish`, `type:architecture`, `type:chore`, `type:research`, or `type:epic`. Area labels locate the affected part of the product: `area:web`, `area:editor`, `area:settings`, `area:api`, `area:engine`, `area:contracts`, `area:design-system`, `area:templates`, `area:integrations`, `area:installer`, or `area:harness`.
52	
53	Milestones are `Pre-merge #151` for work that must land before the feature PR merges, `After merge: evaluate and stabilise` for product evaluation, the architecture sweep and the cutovers they require (this milestone blocks further feature work), and `Later` for queued and long-term work, with most items parked under `backlog`.
54	
55	Epics carry `type:epic` and area labels only; pipelines ignore them. Each child issue starts its body with `Part of #<epic-number>`, and the epic lists its child issues.
56	
57	## Development pipeline
58	
59	An issue is picked up according to its gate label. The implementer named by its `impl:` label works in an isolated branch. The reviewer named by its `review:` label reviews the diff and comes from the opposite model family. A QA agent tests according to the `qa:` label and records results in the PR and the issue. `human-in-the-loop` issues additionally get human QA of the merged build, tracked as described above. `needs-plan-approval` issues get a human-approved plan before implementation. When a human QA step is required before an issue closes (by the label, or by the owner in a comment on the issue), its pull requests reference it as "Part of" rather than "Closes", the pipeline never closes it, and the human who exercised the merged build closes it with a comment saying what was checked.
60	
61	The label names and this process are specific to this repository and are not used by the product's template loops, which users run against their own repositories with their own configurable trigger label and role models (tracked in [the AIDLC template loops epic on GitHub](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Atype%3Aepic%20label%3Aarea%3Atemplates)).

# Five-intent delivery register — 2026-11-17

## Approval and admission

This section records the November 17, 2026 approval and admission snapshot. The linked issues,
PRs and dated [execution checkpoints](2026-11-17-intent-1-execution.md) own subsequent gate,
finding and delivery states; this scope register does not replace their exact-head records.

The owner approved the proposed next batch on November 17, 2026:

> I approve this plan. Send it to the main thread to implement the five intents in order after the macOS launcher, preserving all AIDLC gates and using Claude Code for UI and other implementation work that claude is better suited for, QA, and adversarial review.

The main workflow received the complete handoff and independently read back that user message
in Codex chat `01a1e73c-108c-7333-bb8d-5359783ff9f1`, turn
`01a1eadd-c1e3-7751-94da-a384406a4dd5`, message
`01a1eadd-c2fd-7800-8837-02792093dedc`. The approval and forwarded scope are retained in the
external `2026-11-17-five-intents/owner-approval-receipt.json` delivery record. The prior
recommendation to overlap intent 2 with intent 1 is superseded by this strict sequence.

**Intent 1 admitted on November 17.** The owner subsequently clarified the sequencing:

> Start the five intents now, in order; keep all technical gates (Recommended)

The question explicitly identified that PR #501 remained draft with Mac QA and the dependency
audit blocker unresolved. This answer supersedes only the previous Mac-first admission
dependency. [Recorded owner amendment](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/279#issuecomment-6969001971).
Intent 1 started from main `6d7fcc9838d831fe1be3c3cf52c90a2f33e8f5b1` in isolated worktrees.
The next four intents remain ordered behind it. All review, independent QA, CI, final audit,
merge and owner-acceptance gates remain intact.

At that admission, PR #501 was a separate draft at `6fe12f412cd74b034a77cde10a521bb319e8aa96`
with local Mac QA and its reserved final audit open. CI14 passed native/browser/unit checks but failed the

# 12 - Implementation plan

Milestones are sequential. Each has a goal, the packages it touches, the tasks, and acceptance criteria. "Done" for every milestone includes the definition of done in 10. Sizes are relative: S is days, M is a week or two, L is several weeks for one engineer working with coding agents.

## M0 - Repository and gates (S) - DONE 2026-10-02

Notes: TypeScript 6.x (typescript-eslint does not yet support 7.x), ESLint 10, Vitest 5, Zod 4, pnpm 12. Installation, development, gates and built apps use Node 22 LTS; select it for the whole shell before running commands (ADR-0040).

Goal: an empty monorepo where every CI gate already runs and passes.

Packages: `tooling`, `contracts` skeleton, `domain` skeleton.

Tasks:

1. `pnpm` workspace, Turborepo pipeline, base tsconfig with project references, ESLint, Prettier.
2. dependency-cruiser rules encoding the layer table in 02; a deliberately failing test import to prove the rule fires.
3. Vitest config template with 90/90 thresholds; one real test per skeleton package.
4. Licence allowlist script and the research licence ledger.
5. GitHub Actions workflow with all ten gates; Renovate config.
6. `docs/` linked from the repository README.

Acceptance: CI green on a pull request; a layer violation and a coverage shortfall each fail CI when introduced on purpose.

## M1 - Contracts and domain (M) - DONE 2026-10-02

Notes: the context thread was implemented to the proposed defaults and recorded as ADR-0013 (Draft) rather than waiting for the co-design session. jsonata 2.x keys its evaluation hooks by `Symbol.for('jsonata.__evaluate_entry')`; the time-box relies on that.

Goal: the loop definition, node config schemas, run and event schemas, and the first version of the context thread, with pure validation and thread operations.

Packages: `contracts`, `domain`.

Tasks:

1. Zod schemas for `LoopDefinition`, every node config in 04, `Invocation`, `Run`, `RunEvent`, `ContextThread`.
2. Co-design session on the context thread, closing the five questions in 03 and 13. Record the outcome as ADR-0013.
3. Graph validation with precise, user-facing error messages.
4. Thread operations: JSON Patch apply and validate, every mutation operation in 04, token estimation for truncation.
5. Expression and template evaluation helpers over JSONata and LiquidJS with a sandboxed context object.
6. Exit criteria evaluation, iteration counters, run state machine.
7. Export and import format for definitions.

Acceptance: a definition with every node kind validates; invalid graphs produce the expected errors; property-based tests over patch apply and truncate; coverage above threshold.

## M2 - Engine (L) - DONE 2026-10-02

Notes: all nine handlers, the run manager, fakes for every port, and a scenario helper are in `packages/engine`. Replay-at-node was left for M8. See the implementation notes in 05.

Goal: a run executes end to end against fake ports, including parking, resuming, cancellation, subloops, and crash recovery.

Packages: `engine`.

Tasks:

1. Ports from 02 as interfaces, with in-memory fakes and a fake clock.
2. Run manager: queue, worker pool, status transitions, persisted intents.
3. Executor loop and the node handler contract.
4. Handlers: trigger, decision with the expression strategy, script, mutate, subloop, wait, heartbeat, exit, and inference against the `FakeHarness`.
5. Event store contract and projections.
6. Crash recovery and resume-from-failure.
7. Return channel delivery for `caller`, `event`, `log`, and `file` through the workspace port, `webhook` through the HTTP port.
57:4. Handlers: trigger, decision with the expression strategy, script, mutate, subloop, wait, heartbeat, exit, and inference against the `FakeHarness`.
106:M4 wiring notes (WP-I): `apps/api` composes the Codex and Claude harnesses when no override is given, plus the Codex structured port and deciders `[jev, codex]` (see "Composition" in 06). Claude is available only on supported native Windows setups. `GG_CODEX_BINARY` optionally points at a `codex` executable. Jev reads `jev-api-key` from the local owner's secrets after migrations run at `start()`, and `PUT`/`DELETE /secrets/jev-api-key` refresh it through `Container.onSecretChanged`, so a new key needs no restart. `HarnessPort.resume` takes the full `HarnessStartRequest`, so resumed, repair, and crash-recovery turns keep the node's model, effort, sandbox, and working directory. Session lookup is filtered by harness before selecting the newest eligible session. The SSE stream ends right after the replay when the run is already terminal (07). A `LIVE=1` smoke in `apps/api/src/live.test.ts` runs trigger, Codex inference (`gpt-6-luna`, `low`, read-only), and exit through the API and the real Codex CLI; it passed on 2026-10-03. Jev was verified live on 2026-10-03 with Choice, five-label classification, Noul, direct SDK Score, and a published API loop that succeeded via the Jev route (see `research/jev.md`).
108:M4 extension (#26): the API also registers the owner-installed Claude Code CLI adapter on native Windows. It requires CLI 2.1.285 or newer, required capabilities and `claude.ai` login, uses no Anthropic SDK dependency, and admits the exact supported `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-fable-5-1` models (Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 followed in #206). Claude-specific defaults use `defaults.byHarness.claude`. The accepted policy pairs are read-only/never and explicitly selected danger-full-access/never; this read-only mode is tool-restricted, not OS or filesystem-read confinement. Both models use ordinary technical admission and owner enable switches (ADR-0029). The adapter implementation and focused web gates are recorded in [the #26 QA report](qa/2026-10-07-issue-26.md); full coverage, Edge E2E, the live hostile-config canary, live fresh/resume, and review remain pending.
122:5. Settings: model catalog, defaults, secrets, API keys, harness preflight.
128:Current defaults note (#98): the engine reads owner `defaults.byHarness` as well as loop and process defaults. `GG_DEFAULTS` replaces the old environment variables, and model/effort admission is enforced. The first-pass limitations below are historical.
130:M5 notes (first pass, WP-D): `apps/web` ships tasks 1 to 6; task 7 (adversarial QA) is next. The app is served by the API under `/app/` (`GG_WEB_DIST`), so client routes never collide with API paths. docs/04-node-catalog.md:289:With `returns: "none"` the run finishes without a result and no destination receives anything: neither the exit's own nor those added by the start request's `return`. The engine records no delivery event for them. This is valid configuration, not a failure. A quiet exit is `returns: "none"` with no destinations. A return expression that evaluates to nothing returns `null`, which is a value and is delivered. The exit editor says which case applies, and the inspector states that a run returned nothing by configuration, naming the destinations that received nothing, or identifies the quiet exit (#129, #258).
docs/06-harness-integration.md:716:Windows starts no process whose working directory is missing or longer than 258 characters (error 267). Codex 0.160.0 reports that for a worker command as `CreateProcessWithLogonW failed: 267` (elevated sandbox) or `CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 267` (unelevated). The #102 occurrences came from per-command directories the worker model mistyped, not from GraphGoblin's `--cd`. The Claude and Codex adapters create their `gg-claude-probe-*` and `gg-codex-probe-*` check directories with `mkdir`, because Windows `fs.mkdtemp` fails from 248 characters (247 still works); a name that already exists is never reused or removed, and up to four fresh names are tried. Evidence and the launch comparison matrix: [WP-F5 launch diagnosis](qa/2026-10-19-wp-f5-launch-diagnosis.md).
docs/06-harness-integration.md:999:No readiness probes, probe directories, model selection or fallback policy changed.
docs/10-testing-and-quality.md:117:The Codex readiness probe-directory tests (`packages/adapter-codex/src/probe-directory.test.ts`) run each case as owned work (#466). When Vitest abandons a case after a timeout or a cancelled run, it aborts the test context's signal and goes on to the case's finish hooks while the case body may still be running. The fake CLI runner passes that signal to `runCli`, so the running fake CLI is killed and no further one starts. The finish hook waits for the body, including the adapter's own probe-directory removal, and for every fake CLI process to exit; only then does it restore `TEMP`/`TMP`/`TMPDIR` and remove the case directory, so the next case sees none of its calls. A failure the body reaches after the abort is reported with the timeout. A run cancelled after a case has started but before its body runs, as during its `beforeEach` hooks, still enters the body with the signal already aborted; the case then starts nothing and throws the abort reason, so Vitest reports it as cancelled, as it does the cases it never started. The lifecycle regression cases drive a probe case through a simulated abandonment and are owned the same way: their own Vitest case's abort also abandons the simulated case, and their finish hook waits for the whole test body, including its fault restoration, and finishes the simulated case if an early failure left it unfinished, before the next case starts. A lifecycle test whose case is aborted while its body awaits, before it enters its probe case, ends with the abort reason that the probe case throws on entry: the same object Vitest reports as the case's timeout or cancellation, so the hook does not report it again, while it still reports any other late failure, even one with the same message. Further regression cases enter a probe case and a lifecycle test after their simulated Vitest case was aborted, abort a lifecycle test's own case while its fake CLI runs, and abort a lifecycle test's case while its body awaits before its probe case. The 5 s default timeout and the long-path, collision and creation-fault assertions are unchanged. On Windows the adapter can try to remove its probe directory before a killed fake CLI has released it as its working directory; the adapter then keeps its typed failure and leaves that disposable directory, which the case removes once the process has exited.

Open the worker's Codex session log (`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\sessions`, file name containing the node's session ID) and read that tool call's `workdir`. Check that this `workdir` exists and has at most 258 characters, whether or not it matches the node's working directory (a command may use another directory on purpose). If those paths have 234 characters or more, the Claude check directory exceeds the Windows 258-character working-directory limit: set both to a shorter directory and retry preflight.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

23:562:Composition: `apps/api` builds the Codex adapters from the Codex entry of the harness-keyed process defaults (`GG_DEFAULTS`) and `GG_CODEX_BINARY`, and registers the harness, structured port, Codex structured evaluator and primitive-aware classifier registry. It also registers the Claude harness on supported native Windows hosts using `GG_CLAUDE_BINARY` or the owner-installed CLI path described below. `GG_CODEX_BINARY` remains an optional executable or JavaScript launcher; otherwise the SDK bundled CLI is used. Constructing adapters starts no model session. Old process-default variables are rejected with migration guidance.
24:586:The SDK's event stream ends only when the CLI's stdout closes. A process the CLI started can hold that pipe after the kill, so the adapter waits at most `cancelGraceMs` (5 s, the ADR-0049 harness acknowledgement) after the abort. If the output is still open then, the turn fails `HARNESS_TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` (non-retriable, `delivery-uncertain`) and `cancel()` rejects with the same code, as for the Claude harness; an explicit force therefore ends in `force-failed`. The adapter cannot end that process itself (ADR-0049 N10). POSIX behaviour is unverified on the development machine.
25:706:A saved `none` for GPT-5.5 or a Claude model, like a saved GPT-5.5 `max`, is refused with `EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED` when a draft is saved or published and when Settings or loop defaults are saved, and a run pinned to it fails `EVALUATION_INVALID_CONFIGURATION` (`details.code: EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED`) before any provider request. A Codex/Claude `GG_DEFAULTS` effort its model does not offer stops startup before anything is written, with `EVALUATION_INVALID_CONFIGURATION` and one line per refused harness naming the code, the field, the model and the effort. `minimal` is not an effort at all: a request that names it fails validation, and a stored `minimal` is invalid data, corrected by hand on the contract's typed effort paths (CHANGELOG upgrade note, [ADR-0062](decisions/ADR-0062-stored-data-corrected-by-hand-before-1.0.md)). `details` has one shape for every source of the effort: `code` and `path` (`effort`), and when the effort comes from a default also its `level` (`loop`, `owner` or `process`) and `harness`. Settings offers a Codex default effort only from the model it applies to: the selected default model, or the server default model when none is selected, or the efforts every Codex model shares when neither is known.
27:714:The product owner develops on Windows 11. Codex's native Windows sandbox applies. POSIX signals are not available, so process trees are killed with `taskkill /T /F` where GraphGoblin owns the process (scripts); for Codex sessions the CLI's own job object ends the tree on abort (see "Cancellation"). Every provider and tool process starts with `windowsHide: true` and piped stdio, which gives it its own hidden console: Codex preflight, Claude turns and probes, scripts, and Codex sessions. The SDK 0.160.0 spawns sessions without the option, so a pnpm patch adds it (ADR-0049 acceptance amendment); without it the CLI shared the gateway's console and a terminal Ctrl+C killed a running turn. Paths are normalised with `node:path` and never built by string concatenation.

## Claude Code adapter (#26)

GraphGoblin calls the owner's installed Claude Code CLI directly. It adds no Anthropic SDK or
other Anthropic runtime dependency and never installs, downloads, or bundles the CLI. This
adapter currently supports native Windows only and requires CLI `2.1.285` or newer with all required policy and protocol flags;
older versions, missing capabilities and other operating systems fail closed. `GG_CLAUDE_BINARY` selects an explicit
executable. Otherwise the adapter uses `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe`.

### Authentication and supported models

Preflight and each new or resumed CLI turn run `claude auth status --json` with the adapter's
restricted child environment. Only the `claude.ai` authentication category is accepted. The
response exposes that category, never raw login output, account identity, or credentials. No
GraphGoblin secret stores Claude credentials. Preflight reports the detected CLI version and
missing capabilities, and checks authentication independently even if those checks fail.

The supported models are exact ids; CLI aliases such as `sonnet` or `haiku` are refused. All four
use the same technical readiness, model identity, effort and owner catalog enablement checks
(ADR-0029), and all four seed enabled in the catalog:

| Model id            | Catalog name      | Requested efforts                       | Verification                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `claude-opus-5-5`   | Claude Opus 5.5   | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | Bounded native fresh/resume turns on CLI 2.1.285 ([#26 QA report](qa/2026-10-07-issue-26.md))          |
| `claude-fable-5-1`  | Claude Fable 5.1  | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | Same technical checks as Opus (ADR-0029)                                                               |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | 2026-10-18 on CLI 2.1.292 (#206): direct turns at `low` and `max`; one product turn at `high`          |
| `claude-haiku-5-5`  | Claude Haiku 5.5  | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | 2026-10-18 on CLI 2.1.292 (#206): direct turns at `low`, `xhigh` and `max`; one product turn at `high` |

`none` is not offered for any Claude model: Claude Code 2.1.308 documents `--effort` as `low`,
`medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max` and has no zero-reasoning level, so a saved Claude `none` is
refused with `EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED` like any other unsupported effort. The CLI does not report the
effective effort, so
GraphGoblin records and displays the requested effort and keeps `effectiveEffort` null. Claude
Code documents that a level a model does not support runs at the highest supported level at or
below it; GraphGoblin offers only levels documented for each model, so it expects no such
fallback, but it cannot observe one.

**Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 verification (2026-10-18, #206).** Installed CLI 2.1.292 with a
`claude.ai` login. Each direct turn ran `--print` with a one-line prompt, the adapter's restricted
environment and suppression flags, read-only tools, `--max-turns 1` and `--no-session-persistence`
in a fresh empty temporary directory. Every turn succeeded, and the init record, the assistant
message and the result `modelUsage` all reported exactly the requested id. The product turns ran
one trigger, inference and exit loop per model through the API container's own Claude adapter
(`LIVE_CLAUDE=1 pnpm --filter @graphgoblin/api exec vitest run src/live.test.ts`) with a
disposable data directory; both runs succeeded with `harness.session` recording the requested
model and `high` effort, and the CLI's own session records reported the requested model. The
turn-by-turn results are in the [#206 QA record](qa/2026-10-18-issue-206.md).

Real turns exercised Sonnet 5.5 at `low`, `high` and `max`, and Haiku 5.5 at `low`, `high`,
`xhigh` and `max`. The remaining supported levels, `medium` for both and `xhigh` for Sonnet, rest on
documentation rather than a turn: the CLI 2.1.292 model registry lists effort, `xhigh` and `max`
capabilities for `claude-sonnet-5-5`, and Claude Code's
[model configuration page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config), checked on 2026-10-18,
lists `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max` for both Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. The same page
describes the fallback rule quoted above.

CLI 2.1.292 does not yet list `claude-haiku-5-5` in its model registry. It prints an
`unrecognized_model` notice on stderr, which the adapter does not treat as a refusal (bounded turn
stderr is matched only against the fixed refusal forms below), and treats the model as a
first-party model with every effort level. On 2026-10-23 one real Sonnet 5.5 turn and one real
Haiku 5.5 turn passed again through the built API on Claude Code 2.1.308, which lists both. The
[model configuration page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config), checked on 2026-10-18,
names Claude Code 2.1.293 as the minimum for Haiku 5.5; the turns above passed on 2.1.292, and GraphGoblin keeps its single CLI
minimum (2.1.285) rather than a per-model one. Not admitted: `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, whose
registry entry has no effort capability, so the CLI drops any requested effort (a direct turn at
`max` ran without error, which shows only that the flag is ignored); and `claude-sonnet-5`, the
previous Sonnet.

### Native Windows policy

The supported pairs are `read-only`/`never` and `danger-full-access`/`never`. Read-only enables
the built-in `Read`, `Glob`, and `Grep` tools under the CLI's restricted mode. This is a tool
restriction, not filesystem-read-path or operating-system confinement. Danger-full-access adds
`Edit`, `Write`, and `Bash`; commands and network access are unconfined under the API user's
Windows account. The adapter never promotes another policy to this pair.

`workspace-write`, `on-request`, explicit `networkAccess: false`, `webSearch: true`, nonempty

content.content:
policies keep their existing meanings. Session lookup filters by harness before selecting the
newest matching session, so a Codex session is never passed to Claude or vice versa. The same
resolved request is used for normal and structured-output repair turns. Version, help, and authentication probes run in a fresh empty temporary directory; only the actual turn uses the authored working directory.

The CLI streams JSON lines. GraphGoblin records bounded progress, usage, the transcript artifact,
and a policy-evidence item when transcript capture is enabled. Provider response bodies and raw
stderr are not included in diagnostics. Cancellation owns the CLI process tree; if termination
cannot be confirmed, the run fails with `HARNESS_TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` and is not reported as
cancelled. Engine and persistence failures retain their original cause and stop the active initial or repair session; unconfirmed cleanup takes precedence. Claude is not a decision evaluator: decision evaluation, exit configuration, and
the separate Codex structured port remain unchanged. Inference schema validation uses the authored repair and failure policy for either harness, preserving the native candidate (including null or a missing candidate) rather than substituting final text. API-provider support remains future work tracked by
[#100](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/100).

`system/commands_changed` and `system/ui_invalidate` can precede or follow init. UI invalidation
requires a nonempty string `event` of at most 100 characters and valid UUID-shaped `uuid` and
`session_id`. Both metadata records must use the same session as each other and init. They emit
no progress, session, prompt-delivery or execution evidence. Verified init alone announces the
session. Status, partial-message and rate-limit metadata also carry no execution evidence.
Before init, only init and the two validated metadata records are accepted. After init,
unrecognised record types and system subtypes emit no events or stored evidence. The system
subtypes `hook_started`, `hook_response`, `hook_progress` and `plugin_install` remain refused
at any time. No record may follow the final result.
The sanitised CLI `2.1.287` capture replays all five records through the JSONL parser and
accumulator, including assistant timestamps/request IDs and result timing/terminal/subagent
fields. These additional fields do not alter exact init/result model identity, integer usage,
native structured-candidate selection, tool correlation or native error checks.

Protocol refusals keep `HARNESS_PROTOCOL_ERROR` and identify an unrecognised pre-init record's `type`
and optional `subtype`; policy refusals name the unexpected plugin, skill or tool. Diagnostics
include the detected CLI version and a hint to update GraphGoblin or report that version.
Diagnostic names contain only letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, with a maximum of 100
characters; other values appear as `<invalid>`. Plugin paths and source strings are never
included. Only bounded name-shaped metadata is included, never prompt, response, tool, account or
rate-limit bodies. A green preflight verifies prerequisites; it does not run a model turn or
guarantee that a future CLI stream will pass runtime verification.

The text-input transport supplies no acknowledgement tied to the exact prompt bytes. Session
init and writing stdin are not proof. The adapter does emit `submitted` on validated evidence
that a turn was consumed (below); it does not claim an exact-byte receipt. This is not exact-byte context-delivery proof (#38). Own-session selection follows
#33; it does not invent acceptance evidence.

The earlier [Claude Agent SDK research](research/claude-code-agent-sdk.md) records an alternative
that this adapter does not use.

## Later adapters (recorded)

### LiteLLM

A `LiteLLMPort` would provide plain completion calls for decision, coerce, and summarise operations against local or alternative models. It is not a harness: it has no tools or workspace. It would plug in as a `DeciderPort` and as the provider for the post-1.0 `summarise` operation.

### Submission markers and refusals (#244)

Initialization is session identity, not input acceptance. The engine persists exact pending
prompts and visit provenance before invoking either adapter; see [recovery](05-execution-engine.md#inference-submission-and-recovery).
The run event `harness.submission` says `submitted` with a marker on positive acceptance;
only failed or interrupted turns use the three failure classifications.

| Adapter            | Positive `submitted` marker                                                                                                                                                                                                  | What does not prove acceptance                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude stream-json | First validated non-error `assistant` record producing text, thinking or a tool call (`claude.assistant`); a validated successful `result` record proves consumption when no assistant content was emitted (`claude.result`) | `system/init`, the policy transcript item, commands/UI metadata, status, partial-message and rate-limit records |
| Codex SDK          | `turn.started` (`codex.turn.started`), the input-accepted turn boundary after thread initialization                                                                                                                          | `thread.started`, `resumeThread`, session identity alone, configuration/deprecation error items                 |

Markers emit once per adapter turn. Claude emits `claude.result` as soon as a successful
result record passes session, model, usage and result-text validation, before waiting for CLI exit.
The engine records that acceptance with the visit and turn IDs immediately. Usage totals,
turn completion and the final result still wait for a verified process outcome; a later
transport failure cannot retract the observed acceptance or publish the buffered result.
A lost stream after init or after a marker is uncertain;
markers never claim provider-side durability beyond the observed protocol boundary. A process
kill before the marker is durably recorded remains uncertain too.

Claude local policy/config/auth/readiness failures and confirmed spawn failures are definitely
unsubmitted. Turn stderr is bounded in memory and recognizes only fixed CLI refusal forms:
`error: unknown option` / `error: unexpected argument`, authentication-required diagnostics,
and `No conversation found with session ID:`. Raw diagnostics are discarded. Claude CLI
2.1.304 can emit a pre-init `result` with `is_error: true` and `num_turns: 0` alongside the
missing-session stderr refusal. Before init/acceptance this native refusal result is deferred
until process outcome: the fixed stderr refusal yields `HARNESS_SESSION_MISSING`, ahead of
the otherwise missing-init protocol error. Termination-unconfirmed, abort, timeout and overflow
still take precedence. Without a recognized refusal, a nonzero exit is a generic uncertain
`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`; an otherwise successful process with an incomplete stream remains a
protocol fault. An init/result mismatch also remains a protocol fault. Once assistant acceptance was
observed, later refusal text cannot make the turn definitely unsubmitted.

Codex reports startup/auth/argument refusals as definitely unsubmitted and positively identified
missing-rollout/thread/session refusals as session missing. Other stream/process failures are
uncertain. The engine prevents later refusal from downgrading already observed acceptance.
A provider's refusal of the turn's request (HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`, such as an effort the
model does not accept) is a pinned argument refusal, `HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED`, with the
provider's message. It arrives after `turn.started`, when the CLI has already taken the prompt into
its conversation (its own session history records the turn), so the turn stays accepted and its
provenance stays `delivery-uncertain`; the failure keeps its own non-resumable cause,
`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with `details.adapterCode: HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED`, because sending the
pinned request again would be refused again (#243; [F2 LP-5](qa/2026-10-27-final-f2-live/README.md)).

acceptance is non-resumable when delivery is uncertain (ADR-0045). Accepted turns and
repair/continuation turns on the visit's own session retain continuation recovery. Unsupported
policy, invalid configuration and argument refusals remain non-resumable even if a generic
adapter error incorrectly advertises retryability. Non-pinned generic Codex failures permit
Resume even when the adapter reports `retriable: false` for a CLI exit or lost stream; generic
Claude failures require the adapter's `retriable` evidence. These eligibility rules do not
override D-022's usable-session requirement. Login, installation and quota retain their
restorable causes.

does not positively identify a pre-send refusal. It does not authorize a blind authored retry.

tool_use_result.stdout:
policies keep their existing meanings. Session lookup filters by harness before selecting the
newest matching session, so a Codex session is never passed to Claude or vice versa. The same
resolved request is used for normal and structured-output repair turns. Version, help, and authentication probes run in a fresh empty temporary directory; only the actual turn uses the authored working directory.

The CLI streams JSON lines. GraphGoblin records bounded progress, usage, the transcript artifact,
and a policy-evidence item when transcript capture is enabled. Provider response bodies and raw
stderr are not included in diagnostics. Cancellation owns the CLI process tree; if termination
cannot be confirmed, the run fails with `HARNESS_TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` and is not reported as
cancelled. Engine and persistence failures retain their original cause and stop the active initial or repair session; unconfirmed cleanup takes precedence. Claude is not a decision evaluator: decision evaluation, exit configuration, and
the separate Codex structured port remain unchanged. Inference schema validation uses the authored repair and failure policy for either harness, preserving the native candidate (including null or a missing candidate) rather than substituting final text. API-provider support remains future work tracked by
[#100](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/100).

`system/commands_changed` and `system/ui_invalidate` can precede or follow init. UI invalidation
requires a nonempty string `event` of at most 100 characters and valid UUID-shaped `uuid` and
`session_id`. Both metadata records must use the same session as each other and init. They emit
no progress, session, prompt-delivery or execution evidence. Verified init alone announces the
session. Status, partial-message and rate-limit metadata also carry no execution evidence.
Before init, only init and the two validated metadata records are accepted. After init,
unrecognised record types and system subtypes emit no events or stored evidence. The system
subtypes `hook_started`, `hook_response`, `hook_progress` and `plugin_install` remain refused
at any time. No record may follow the final result.
The sanitised CLI `2.1.287` capture replays all five records through the JSONL parser and
accumulator, including assistant timestamps/request IDs and result timing/terminal/subagent
fields. These additional fields do not alter exact init/result model identity, integer usage,
native structured-candidate selection, tool correlation or native error checks.

Protocol refusals keep `HARNESS_PROTOCOL_ERROR` and identify an unrecognised pre-init record's `type`
and optional `subtype`; policy refusals name the unexpected plugin, skill or tool. Diagnostics
include the detected CLI version and a hint to update GraphGoblin or report that version.
Diagnostic names contain only letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, with a maximum of 100
characters; other values appear as `<invalid>`. Plugin paths and source strings are never
included. Only bounded name-shaped metadata is included, never prompt, response, tool, account or
rate-limit bodies. A green preflight verifies prerequisites; it does not run a model turn or
guarantee that a future CLI stream will pass runtime verification.

The text-input transport supplies no acknowledgement tied to the exact prompt bytes. Session
init and writing stdin are not proof. The adapter does emit `submitted` on validated evidence
that a turn was consumed (below); it does not claim an exact-byte receipt. This is not exact-byte context-delivery proof (#38). Own-session selection follows
#33; it does not invent acceptance evidence.

The earlier [Claude Agent SDK research](research/claude-code-agent-sdk.md) records an alternative
that this adapter does not use.

## Later adapters (recorded)

### LiteLLM

A `LiteLLMPort` would provide plain completion calls for decision, coerce, and summarise operations against local or alternative models. It is not a harness: it has no tools or workspace. It would plug in as a `DeciderPort` and as the provider for the post-1.0 `summarise` operation.

### Submission markers and refusals (#244)

Initialization is session identity, not input acceptance. The engine persists exact pending
prompts and visit provenance before invoking either adapter; see [recovery](05-execution-engine.md#inference-submission-and-recovery).
The run event `harness.submission` says `submitted` with a marker on positive acceptance;
only failed or interrupted turns use the three failure classifications.

| Adapter            | Positive `submitted` marker                                                                                                                                                                                                  | What does not prove acceptance                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude stream-json | First validated non-error `assistant` record producing text, thinking or a tool call (`claude.assistant`); a validated successful `result` record proves consumption when no assistant content was emitted (`claude.result`) | `system/init`, the policy transcript item, commands/UI metadata, status, partial-message and rate-limit records |
| Codex SDK          | `turn.started` (`codex.turn.started`), the input-accepted turn boundary after thread initialization                                                                                                                          | `thread.started`, `resumeThread`, session identity alone, configuration/deprecation error items                 |

Markers emit once per adapter turn. Claude emits `claude.result` as soon as a successful
result record passes session, model, usage and result-text validation, before waiting for CLI exit.
The engine records that acceptance with the visit and turn IDs immediately. Usage totals,
turn completion and the final result still wait for a verified process outcome; a later
transport failure cannot retract the observed acceptance or publish the buffered result.
A lost stream after init or after a marker is uncertain;
markers never claim provider-side durability beyond the observed protocol boundary. A process
kill before the marker is durably recorded remains uncertain too.

Claude local policy/config/auth/readiness failures and confirmed spawn failures are definitely
unsubmitted. Turn stderr is bounded in memory and recognizes only fixed CLI refusal forms:

missing-session stderr refusal. Before init/acceptance this native refusal result is deferred
until process outcome: the fixed stderr refusal yields `HARNESS_SESSION_MISSING`, ahead of
the otherwise missing-init protocol error. Termination-unconfirmed, abort, timeout and overflow
still take precedence. Without a recognized refusal, a nonzero exit is a generic uncertain
`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`; an otherwise successful process with an incomplete stream remains a
protocol fault. An init/result mismatch also remains a protocol fault. Once assistant acceptance was
observed, later refusal text cannot make the turn definitely unsubmitted.

Codex reports startup/auth/argument refusals as definitely unsubmitted and positively identified
missing-rollout/thread/session refusals as session missing. Other stream/process failures are
uncertain. The engine prevents later refusal from downgrading already observed acceptance.
A provider's refusal of the turn's request (HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`, such as an effort the

Check that this `workdir` exists and has at most 258 characters, whether or not it matches the node's working directory (a command may use another directory on purpose). A `workdir` that drops a segment of the node's directory is a probable typo by the worker, as in the diagnosed case, and needs no GraphGoblin change. # Changelog

All notable changes to GraphGoblin. The design is in [docs/](docs/README.md); the user guide is [docs/guide/](docs/guide/README.md).

## Unreleased

- Windows launcher identity and ownership checks own their descendants in private Windows jobs
  (#459), drain both output streams within a bounded work window and collect failed checks
  before displaying errors. Initial checks retain the 15-second work cap, with up to two seconds
  for cleanup; held-store retries reserve that cleanup time and retain the last held guidance
  when a conclusive new sample cannot fit. Raw helper output is never displayed or logged.
  Ownership output is parsed once as strict JSON before whitespace normalization; duplicate
  decoded keys, unknown fields and JavaScript-only syntax refuse startup. Cleanup is confirmed
  only when the complete process/job/stream observation finishes before the two-second deadline;
  a later completion keeps the unconfirmed-cleanup outcome (D166).
  Caller admission now carries one absolute work cutoff through helper preparation, creation,
  validation and result consumption. Setup cannot restart the held retry's clock or admit a
  free sample inside its reserved cleanup interval; equality at the cutoff refuses (D167).
  **Upgrade:** rebuild and reinstall the launcher. Windows 10 or Windows Server 2016 or later
  with compatible nested jobs is required, including for warm shortcut clicks. A restricted host
  can refuse the shortcut while an existing gateway remains callable at its current address.
  No store, lock or export format change and no reset. PR #460 remains separately held.

- API startup now prints one stack-free line for held or unverifiable data-directory,
  SQLite-file and reclamation ownership, with exit code 1 (#409). It keeps the lock path and
  verification reason, gives guidance for live and unknown owners, and escapes control characters
  and line separators in the explanation. Lock records, acquisition rules, managed startup
  categories and unrelated diagnostics are unchanged.

- `--reset` manifests and output account for both writer locks and their `.reclaim` guards
  (#434). The dry run and the confirmed manifest list `<database-file>.graphgoblin.lock` and
  `graphgoblin.lock` as the reset's own locks, removed on release, where the confirmed manifest
  previously listed its own database lock under Keeps as unrelated data. A stale lock file or
  `.reclaim` guard is listed as reclaimed when the reset takes that lock, instead of being kept
  (the database lock and its guard) or omitted (the data-directory guard); the stale lock of

**Start refusals (#364).** A spawn `ENOENT` does not say which operand failed: on Windows 11 with
Node 22.23.4, a missing working directory, one that is a file and an existing one longer than 258
characters are all refused with the same `ENOENT` as a missing executable, and Node attributes
each to the executable. After an actual refusal (Node created no process), the runner makes one
read-only observation of the request's own executable and working directory and returns only a
closed cause. The executable counts as missing only when its configured path is fully qualified
and that path and its `.com` and `.exe` forms, the names Windows process start tries, are all
absent or folders; an executable named without a full path is never resolved through `PATH`. A
working directory that is absent (or below a file) or is not a folder is established from its own
metadata. An existing folder establishes nothing, because it can still be unstartable, and a read
that fails for any other reason leaves the cause unknown. The adapter reports only what was
established, in fixed text without paths:

| Established                              | Preflight                                                                                                                                                             | Turn                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Executable missing                       | `cli-missing`: "Claude CLI was not found at the configured path."                                                                                                     | `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` (restorable), raised by the turn's own readiness check                                                             |
| Turn working directory missing or a file | Not applicable                                                                                                                                                        | `HARNESS_INVALID_CONFIGURATION`: "Claude could not be started because the working directory does not exist" (or "is not a folder"), pinned |
| Check folder missing or a file           | `unknown`: "Claude CLI could not be started because its temporary check folder does not exist." (or "is not a folder")                                                | The same detail as `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`; the check folder is never configuration                                                          |
| Nothing, path over 258 characters        | `unknown`: "... from its temporary check folder, whose path (from TEMP or TMP) is longer than the 258 characters Windows allows for a working directory."                | `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`: "Claude could not be started (ENOENT); the working directory path is longer than the 258 characters Windows allows" |
| Nothing                                  | `unknown`: "Claude CLI could not be started (ENOENT)." (or the `EACCES`/`UNKNOWN` code)                                                                                | `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`: "Claude could not be started (ENOENT); check the Claude executable's path and permissions and the working directory" |

Every refusal stays `definitely-not-submitted`, and the turn uses the working directory exactly as
given. Unconfirmed termination and cancellation keep their precedence; an abort or deadline that
arrives during the observation reports the refusal at once, without a cause and without a timeout.
A later error event of a started process, such as a failed kill, is not a refusal. From 260
characters Windows also fails the refused process's stdout and stderr pipes (`read ENOTCONN`); the
runner ignores pipe faults of a process that never started, where they previously escaped as an
uncaught exception. A started process's stdout or stderr failure stops its tree and fails the turn
(`HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`, delivery uncertain) or the check ("Claude CLI check output could not be
read."). The 258-character wording states the path's length against the documented limit; it is
not proof of the cause.

# 06 - Harness integration

Each inference node selects its harness through `config.harness`, defaulting to `codex`.
Loop settings supply per-harness model and effort defaults; loop-level harness input is rejected.
Decision routes and temporary boolean predicates use the Codex decider; structured repair uses the structured-completion port. See
[ADR-0019](decisions/ADR-0019-inference-node-harness.md) and
[ADR-0023](decisions/ADR-0023-installed-claude-code.md).

## Native Chat workflow integration (#443)

Native Chat is an entry point into the existing engine, not a second inference implementation.
The gateway seeds one system loop with **Trigger → Inference → Context mutation → Exit**. It uses normal harness
selection, model/effort defaults and readiness checks. The inference captures plain text; the
ordinary Context mutation constructs the exact response envelope deterministically.
Seeding and device pairing make no provider request and do not silently choose a discovered model.
Each turn pins the published definition and effective defaults through native admission.
Missing CLI/authentication/model prerequisites produce actionable readiness before a new turn is
admitted; there is no substitute reply or provider failover.
The minimal system seed can exist published before model setup; it cannot send until ready.

The seeded inference node starts a fresh session in a temporary working directory. Its prompt
receives the current text and server-built bounded conversation history. The existing harness
policy applies: [ADR-0063](decisions/ADR-0063-loop-turns-without-personal-extensions.md) is amended
by [ADR-0067](decisions/ADR-0067-codex-inherits-configured-plugins.md), so Codex inherits configured
plugins and their tools/services while standalone MCP discovery and other isolation defaults remain.
Owners may edit the workflow's interior, including its harness, prompt, model, effort,
scripts, decisions and awaited subloops. Native Chat does not sandbox arbitrary owner-authored
Script commands or introduce a smart-home routing provider. Guided transcription is an ordinary
Script normalizer described below.

The loop boundary uses the canonical `graphgoblin.chat.v1` input schema from
`packages/contracts/src/chat.ts`. The server supplies `conversationId`, `requestId`, turn counter,
current input and recent valid history. A text input is `{kind: 'text', text}`. An audio input is
`{kind: 'audio', audio: {id, mimeType, bytes, path}, caption?}`; only the server can resolve the private
absolute path. A client sends an upload id, never a path or URL. The server limits history to the
most recent twelve valid completed turn pairs and 64,000 characters, dropping oldest whole pairs.

The boundary requires one manual trigger named `chat-input`, exposed to exactly UI and API, and
the canonical `chatResponse` variable schema. The deterministic Context mutation writes the
response into `/vars/chatResponse`. Every successful exit returns exactly `vars.chatResponse` to
exactly the caller. Failure/exhausted exits may return none or that same canonical response; they
never become successful assistant messages. The public response is exactly
`{protocol: 'graphgoblin.chat.v1', reply: '<nonblank text>'}`. Strings, `text`, `message` and arbitrary
JSON are not reply aliases. The chat projection validates a successful native result again on
read, so an invalid result is `CHAT_RESPONSE_INVALID` without a reply or future-history entry.

Draft saves refuse changes to the locked trigger identity/type/exposure/canonical schema and the
`chatResponse` variable schema. Other boundary wiring issues remain saveable and block
publication/admission. A generic system-loop start, draft test or Subloop accepts text-only
protocol input, even when its published loop supports audio. Only native chat admission resolves
a new audio reference. Verified immutable native replay may retain the source audio; a new start
or caller-supplied replay id cannot grant path authority.

### Configure an audio normalizer

Audio is unavailable in the default text-only loop. To enable it, replace the trigger input schema
with the exported canonical audio-capable schema and make `chat-normalize` the only node directly
after `chat-input`. Use one of these native node configurations:

| Node    | Required configuration                                                                       | Recorded text                                                                                 |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Script  | `stdin: 'thread'`, `stdout: 'last-output'`; return JSON `{text}`                             | `thread.outputs['chat-normalize'].value.text`                                                 |
| Subloop | `output.mode: 'result-only'`, `output.resultTo.lastOutput: true`; the child returns `{text}` | `thread.outputs['chat-normalize'].value.result.text`, with its envelope `status: 'succeeded'` |

Successful Script output continues to the protected check. Unhandled exit codes fail normally;
an existing explicit exit-code mapping to `out` retains its native meaning.

The normalizer must handle text pass-through as well as audio transcription. The protected chain
is `chat-input.out → chat-normalize.out → chat-normalize-check`: the canonical expression decision
continues through `valid` into the authored workflow or through `invalid` into the failure exit
`chat-normalize-invalid` (`outcome: 'failure'`, `returns: 'none'`, no destinations). Input, normalizer
and check cannot be revisited or bypassed; the failure exit accepts only that invalid edge.
The check validates the original recorded Script object or succeeded Subloop result before a
later model/action runs. It requires exactly one key, `text`, whose nonblank string is at most
16,000 UTF-16 code units. Unknown fields, blank/overlength text and a malformed Subloop envelope
fail without continuing to later actions. Expression errors fail safely too; no coercion/repair
changes transcript content.

Use the domain's `enableChatAudio(definition, normalizer)` and `disableChatAudio(definition)`
helpers to change the canonical trigger/normalizer/check/failure chain as one edit. Enabling refuses
ambiguous continuation wiring and reserved-id collisions. Disabling can also remove a partial
chain: it uses exactly one valid existing check continuation, or requires an explicit
`{continuationNodeId}` naming an ordinary nontrigger step (`SYSTEM_CHAT_CONTINUATION_REQUIRED`).
It removes reserved voice nodes/incident edges and existing trigger-outgoing edges, restores one
trigger continuation and leaves other ordinary nodes/edges intact. For the exact untouched seed prompt,
they also switch its input reference; they do not rewrite arbitrary owner prompts. Custom
interiors must consume the recorded normalized text described above. Subloops already await their
child; do not add a `wait` property or change the native subloop result envelope. The projector
selects the extractor from the pinned node kind and independently validates the recorded value.
The owner editor exposes these edits as **Set up voice messages**, **Add voice steps** and
**Turn off voice messages**. Setup stages a real Script/Subloop configuration without executing
it; publication remains a separate action.

The normalized text must contain 1–16,000 nonblank UTF-16 code units. For an audio turn, a successful raw
run without a valid recorded normalizer result becomes `CHAT_AUDIO_NORMALIZATION_INVALID` and
does not display a reply or enter future history. A model-generated guess is never a transcript.
The session's **Configured by loop** state establishes this static contract only: an unavailable
